quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Drive off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, do not slam on the brakes or make sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely, whether they are in a marked crosswalk or not. Always yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
A small car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, and van drivers may not see you directly behind them. Large vehicles can also block your view of the road ahead. Increase your following distance with these vehicles so you can see around them.

questions.question: You park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the edge, not into traffic.

questions.question: When parked facing uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parked facing uphill without a curb or facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Avoid the brakes and let the car slow on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically faster than you can.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes and shift to neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: In a skid, release the brakes and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left to straighten the vehicle.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege that you must earn and keep. It is not a right.

questions.question: Before making a left turn from a two-way street, position your car:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: For a left turn from a two-way street, start in the lane nearest the centerline. Turn when the front of your car reaches the intersection center. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane available.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never, it confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space before you move back into the driving lane. You need enough room between your car and the car you passed. When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the driving lane.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you turn left, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles moving on their green light.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind while moving, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against the back of your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what should you do?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge to the right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to upcoming dangers. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind while moving, your body will be thrown backward. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and pushing your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: If you cannot see clearly at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: You must slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, you should stop and move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.question: When driving on a road with a single broken white centerline, what can you do?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic is moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you while driving.
Keep your eyes moving to watch for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to watch for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: You drive defensively when you look ahead for potential hazards. Staring only at the road directly in front of your car is dangerous. Scan ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: A red light is showing, but a police officer tells you to drive through the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Drive through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer directing traffic always overrides traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: At an intersection with a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and continue without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicles crossing or merging that are close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep your instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day. You cannot see as far ahead at night. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. This gives you the safest path between both dangers.

questions.question: Dust or smoke is blocking your view of other vehicles. What should you turn on besides slowing down?

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever conditions make it hard to see other vehicles. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where animals, people, and vehicles may cross the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as for normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Only slow down if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers safe.
